# Installation

Prebuilt binaries support Linux x86-64 (`amd64`) and ARM64 with glibc 2.36+,
PAM and the system's PAM/NSS configuration, including Debian 12+ and Ubuntu 24.04+.
They do not support Alpine/musl or 32-bit systems. Go and Node are not needed
to run them. For the container, see [Docker setup](guide.md#docker).

## Install script

Install or update to the latest stable release:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://tuxee.agent-zero.ai/install.sh | sudo sh
```

Or select a version:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://tuxee.agent-zero.ai/install.sh | sudo sh -s -- v1.2.3
```

Omit `sudo` when already root. The installer needs curl and sha256sum.
It verifies the download and installs `tuxee` in `/usr/local/bin` without
starting or restarting it. If that directory is missing from your PATH, run:

```sh
export PATH="/usr/local/bin:$PATH"
```

Add that line to your shell profile if needed.

### Update an older installation

Rerun the same install command, even if the installed version has no
`tuxee update` command. The script runs the downloaded binary's installer.
It replaces an existing Tuxee binary at `/usr/local/lib/tuxee/tuxee` (the default
systemd service location) or `/usr/local/bin/tuxee`, preserving configuration,
state and the service unit. Repeating the command is safe; unrelated files
are refused.

The running server keeps its old version until restarted. When ready, restart
the default service:

```sh
sudo /usr/local/bin/tuxee restart
```

Restarting ends all terminal sessions. For a foreground server, stop it and run
`/usr/local/bin/tuxee serve` with its original options. Custom executable paths
and custom-named service copies are separate installations; this command updates
only the default installation.

## Manual binary installation

Download the binary and checksum from the same
[GitHub release](https://github.com/agent0ai/tuxee/releases). These commands
select the latest release; replace the `tag=...` line with `tag=v1.2.3` to choose
a specific version.

```sh
(
    set -eu
    case "$(uname -m)" in
        x86_64|amd64) arch=amd64 ;;
        aarch64|arm64) arch=arm64 ;;
        *) echo "Supported architectures: x86-64 and ARM64." >&2; exit 1 ;;
    esac
    release=$(curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' \
        --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 30 -o /dev/null -w '%{url_effective}' \
        https://github.com/agent0ai/tuxee/releases/latest)
    tag=${release##*/}
    asset=tuxee-linux-$arch
    base=https://github.com/agent0ai/tuxee/releases/download/$tag
    stage=$(mktemp -d)
    trap 'rm -rf "$stage"' EXIT
    cd "$stage"
    curl -fSL --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' --connect-timeout 10 \
        --max-time 120 --max-filesize 134217728 -o "$asset" "$base/$asset"
    curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' --connect-timeout 10 \
        --max-time 30 --max-filesize 1048576 -o checksums.txt "$base/checksums.txt"
    awk -v name="$asset" '$2 == name' checksums.txt > selected-checksum.txt
    sha256sum --check --strict selected-checksum.txt
    chmod 700 "$asset"
    [ "$("./$asset" version)" = "Tuxee ${tag#v}" ]
    sudo "./$asset" __install
)
```

The final command invokes the binary's installer. It safely replaces an existing
Tuxee executable, preserves configuration, and refuses unrelated commands at the
installation path. Installation uses `/usr/local/lib/tuxee/tuxee` with a symlink
at `/usr/local/bin/tuxee`. Neither installation method restarts a running server.

## Run

```sh
sudo tuxee serve
```

Open `https://SERVER/` and sign in with an existing Linux username and password.
Private addresses use a local certificate; see [HTTPS setup](guide.md#https).
Root is required to authenticate Linux users and run their shells with their
own permissions.

On a system with a running systemd manager, register boot startup and start:

```sh
sudo tuxee service install
sudo tuxee start
```

Other systems can run `tuxee serve` through their existing supervisor.
See [service management](guide.md#native-service) and [updates](releases.md#update).
Restarting Tuxee ends its terminal sessions.

## Advanced: build from source

Requires Linux, Go 1.26.3+, Node 22+, a C compiler and PAM development headers.
On Debian/Ubuntu, install the native build dependencies:

```sh
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install git build-essential libpam0g-dev
```

With Go and Node on PATH:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/agent0ai/tuxee.git
cd tuxee
npm ci
npm run build
go build -trimpath -o bin/tuxee ./cmd/tuxee
sudo ./bin/tuxee serve
```

Build the frontend before Go builds or tests on a fresh checkout. The result
includes the web UI; Node is not required at runtime. The executable links to
the build system's glibc and PAM, so build on a compatible system.

To install the source build as a boot service:

```sh
sudo ./bin/tuxee service install
sudo ./bin/tuxee start
```

See the [developer guide](guide.md#build-and-run) for isolated local runs and
[verification commands](guide.md#verification).

# Purpose

Detailed product, deployment and development documentation.

# Ownership

`install.md` owns the installer,
manual binary download/installation commands, and advanced Go compilation.
`guide.md` owns deployment, interaction, verification and implementation limits.
`releases.md` owns updates, GitHub/Docker Hub setup and publication limits.
Root `README.md` owns the logo/title, short container/standalone introduction,
illustrated Highlights, Quick start, Resources links and Agent Zero credits.

# Local Contracts

Run documented shell commands from the repository root unless stated otherwise.
Resolve documentation links relative to their containing file.
Keep verified behavior separate from limitations; do not claim checks ran merely
because their commands are documented.

# Work Guidance

Keep operational details here and link them from the root README.

# Verification

Use the build commands in `install.md` and verification commands in `guide.md`.

# Purpose

Real-system integration and browser verification.

# Ownership

This document owns this subtree.

# Local Contracts

Use dedicated test users, temporary fixtures and isolated listener ports. Never log passwords. Test the real server/PTY/filesystem rather than replacing it with mocks. Systemd and Docker runtime checks require those facilities to be available.

# Work Guidance

Keep implementation and checks small and complete.

# Verification

- `npm run test:updates`: start an isolated real server and use the marked account; cover the GitHub link, update-row placement directly below the version, one-line desktop summary, local check-time format, manual checks, cached polling, About/hamburger badges, highlighted updates visible without scrolling, command-only guidance, retained warnings/timestamps on errors, cleared highlights after recovery, desktop/mobile light/dark bounds, no external browser requests and logout cleanup. Restore settings. Run sequentially with other account tests.
- `TUXEE_SYSTEM_TEST=1 go test ./tests -run TestRunningServerKeepsHelpersAfterBinaryReplacement`: atomically replace a disposable running executable with an incompatible fixture; verify real PAM, file helpers and the retained PTY identity continue.

- `node tests/terminal-lost.mjs`: create/delete a real PTY behind a saved layout, then check centered “Terminal session lost” and the primary Restart terminal button on a uniform theme-colored surface. Capture desktop/mobile screenshots in dark/light mode, verify the renderer is hidden, restart creates/persists a working shell, backend closure uses the same recovery view and normal process exit retains output. Use a marked account (`TUXEE_TEST_USER` can select an isolated one), restore settings and remove only test-created terminals.
- `node tests/connection.mjs`: start/restart an isolated real server with SIGTERM; use real PAM/API/Chromium, a marked account, a temporary draft file and restored settings. In a file-only workspace with monitoring hidden, check offline/server/proxy loss, stalled-probe timeout, healthy operation errors, dark/light/mobile blur and spinner, reduced motion, modal/Escape blocking and unchanged editor DOM/draft after recovery. Invalid readiness responses (404/HTML/malformed JSON/401/missing state) cannot show login; unrelated 401 must trigger readiness verification. Check delayed expiry after a newer disconnect or login, actual restart-to-login timing, first sign-in after restart, unavailable startup, login-screen monitoring, friendly protocol errors and no credential replay. Assert the original dashboard/editor survives until a valid current readiness response. Browser routes inject transport/protocol faults; application, file reads and authentication use the real server. Run sequentially with other account-based suites.

- `node tests/retained.mjs`: real PAM/API/Chromium checks for terminals missing from all workspace layouts, including sessions attached elsewhere. Check inactive-workspace exclusion, running-only warnings on both the menu item and hamburger, Attach preserving PID and saved identity, cancelled/confirmed termination, ended-session cleanup, closed-menu discovery, mobile/light rendering, inventory errors and logout cleanup. With Tini on PATH, run the production entrypoint with fixture services to check parallel startup, foreground/restart-loop hooks, clean/crash restarts with a delay, no hook duplication, and INT/TERM process-group shutdown including delayed service cleanup. # Purpose

Read-only Linux resource monitoring for the authenticated dashboard.

# Ownership

Own cached CPU, memory, swap, mounted-filesystem and network samples. HTTP admission and per-user display preferences belong to server; presentation belongs to web.

# Local Contracts

- Share one sample across callers for two seconds. CPU and network rates use counter deltas; initial/reset counters produce unavailable rates, never fabricated spikes.
- Return the reserved `/all` network first, summing counters and measured rates of interfaces whose operstate is `up` or `unknown`, including loopback and virtual interfaces. Sum per-interface rates, never deltas of changing aggregate counters; an unavailable member rate makes that direction unavailable. No active interfaces yield zero; a failed counter read yields no networks. Do not truncate discovery before aggregating.
- Native mode reports the host. Containers read their own cgroup v1/v2 accounting and effective visible CPU/memory limits. Never replace unavailable container accounting with host usage.
- Disk capacity is per visible local filesystem, not a sum across bind mounts or container writable-layer size. Skip remote/pseudo filesystems and file bind mounts. Inputs come from kernel mount discovery, never client-supplied paths.
- No processes, addresses, environment contents or credentials are exposed. No external service, agent, database or new dependency is required.

# Work Guidance

Use the kernel's documented interfaces: [/proc](https://docs.kernel.org/filesystems/proc.html), [cgroup v2](https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/cgroup-v2.html), [v1 memory](https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/cgroup-v1/memory.html), [network counters](https://docs.kernel.org/networking/statistics.html), [operational states](https://docs.kernel.org/networking/operstates.html).

# Verification

name: Release Tuxee

on:
  push:
    tags: ['v*']

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: tuxee-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  IMAGE: ${{ vars.DOCKERHUB_IMAGE || 'agent0ai/tuxee' }}
  TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}

jobs:
  build:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - arch: amd64
            runner: ubuntu-24.04
          - arch: arm64
            runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Validate release inputs
        env:
          DOCKERHUB_ORG: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_ORG }}
          DOCKERHUB_OAT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_OAT_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          python3 .github/release-notes.py "$TAG" > /tmp/release-notes.md
          test -n "$DOCKERHUB_ORG" && test -n "$DOCKERHUB_OAT_TOKEN" || {
            echo "::error::Set DOCKERHUB_ORG and DOCKERHUB_OAT_TOKEN repository secrets."
            exit 1
          }
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - name: Verify
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -qq
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends libpam0g-dev
          npm ci
          npm run build
          mkdir -p bin
          go build -o bin/tuxee ./cmd/tuxee
          go test ./internal/... ./cmd/... ./tests
          sudo env TUXEE_SYSTEM_TEST=1 GOMAXPROCS=2 "$(command -v go)" test -p 2 ./internal/identity ./tests
          go vet ./internal/... ./cmd/... ./tests
          python3 .github/release-notes.py --self-test
          npm run test:installer
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_ORG }}
          password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_OAT_TOKEN }}
      - name: Build and push native image by digest
        id: image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          platforms: linux/${{ matrix.arch }}
          build-args: VERSION=${{ github.ref_name }}
          outputs: type=image,name=${{ env.IMAGE }},push-by-digest=true,name-canonical=true,push=true
          cache-from: type=gha,scope=release-${{ matrix.arch }}
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max,scope=release-${{ matrix.arch }}
      - name: Export the matching release binary
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          target: binary
          platforms: linux/${{ matrix.arch }}
          build-args: VERSION=${{ github.ref_name }}
          outputs: type=local,dest=release
          cache-from: type=gha,scope=release-${{ matrix.arch }}
      - name: Verify image and binary
        env:
          ARCH: ${{ matrix.arch }}
          DIGEST: ${{ steps.image.outputs.digest }}
        run: |
          mv release/tuxee "release/tuxee-linux-$ARCH"
          chmod +x "release/tuxee-linux-$ARCH"
          test "$("release/tuxee-linux-$ARCH" version)" = "Tuxee ${TAG#v}"
          # Hosted runners make /usr/local/bin world-writable for tool installation.
          sudo install -d -o root -g root -m 0755 /usr/local/bin
          sudo "release/tuxee-linux-$ARCH" __install
          sudo "release/tuxee-linux-$ARCH" __install
          test "$(/usr/local/bin/tuxee version)" = "Tuxee ${TAG#v}"
          docker pull "$IMAGE@$DIGEST"
          test "$(docker run --rm --entrypoint /usr/local/bin/tuxee "$IMAGE@$DIGEST" version)" = "Tuxee ${TAG#v}"
          mkdir -p digests
          touch "digests/${DIGEST#sha256:}"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: binary-${{ matrix.arch }}
          path: release/tuxee-linux-*
          if-no-files-found: error
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: digest-${{ matrix.arch }}
          path: digests/*
          if-no-files-found: error

  publish:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: binary-*
          path: release
          merge-multiple: true
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: digest-*
          path: digests
          merge-multiple: true
      - name: Prepare release assets and notes
        run: |
          test -f release/tuxee-linux-amd64
          test -f release/tuxee-linux-arm64
          (cd release && sha256sum tuxee-linux-* > checksums.txt)
          python3 .github/release-notes.py "$TAG" > release-notes.md
      - name: Prepare draft
        id: release
        uses: actions/github-script@v8
        with:
          script: |
            const fs = require('fs');
            const {owner, repo} = context.repo;
            const tag = process.env.TAG;
            const version = s => {
              if (!/^v(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$/.test(s)) throw new Error('Invalid stable tag');
              return s.slice(1).split('.').map(BigInt);
            };
            let latest = true;
            try {
              const current = version((await github.rest.repos.getLatestRelease({owner, repo})).data.tag_name);
              const next = version(tag);
              latest = next.some((n, i) => n > current[i] && next.slice(0, i).every((v, j) => v === current[j]));
            } catch (error) { if (error.status !== 404) throw error; }
            let release;
            try {
              release = (await github.rest.repos.getReleaseByTag({owner, repo, tag})).data;
              if (!release.draft) throw new Error('Refusing to overwrite a published release');
            } catch (error) {
              if (error.status !== 404) throw error;
              release = (await github.rest.repos.createRelease({
                owner, repo, tag_name: tag, name: `Tuxee ${tag}`, draft: true,
                body: fs.readFileSync('release-notes.md', 'utf8')
              })).data;
            }
            core.setOutput('id', release.id);
            core.setOutput('latest', String(latest));
      - name: Upload verified binaries
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: gh release upload "$TAG" release/* --clobber
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_ORG }}
          password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_OAT_TOKEN }}
      - name: Publish both image platforms
        env:
          MAKE_LATEST: ${{ steps.release.outputs.latest }}
        run: |
          tags=(-t "$IMAGE:$TAG" -t "$IMAGE:${TAG#v}")
          if [ "$MAKE_LATEST" = true ]; then tags+=(-t "$IMAGE:latest"); fi
          sources=()
          for digest in digests/*; do sources+=("$IMAGE@sha256:${digest##*/}"); done
          test "${#sources[@]}" -eq 2
          docker buildx imagetools create "${tags[@]}" "${sources[@]}"
      - name: Publish complete GitHub release
        uses: actions/github-script@v8
        env:
          RELEASE_ID: ${{ steps.release.outputs.id }}
          MAKE_LATEST: ${{ steps.release.outputs.latest }}
        with:
          script: |
            await github.rest.repos.updateRelease({
              ...context.repo, release_id: Number(process.env.RELEASE_ID),
              draft: false, make_latest: process.env.MAKE_LATEST
            });

#!/bin/sh
# Install or update Tuxee; the installed version need not support updates.
# curl -fsSL https://tuxee.agent-zero.ai/install.sh | sudo sh -s -- [v1.2.3]
set -eu

main() {
    if [ "$#" -gt 1 ]; then
        echo 'Usage: install.sh [vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH]' >&2
        exit 2
    fi
    case "${1:-}" in --help|-h)
        echo 'Usage: install.sh [vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH]'
        echo 'Install or update Tuxee (latest stable by default). Does not restart it.'
        return ;;
    esac
    [ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || { echo 'Run with sudo sh, or as root.' >&2; exit 1; }
    [ "$(uname -s)" = Linux ] || { echo 'Tuxee requires Linux.' >&2; exit 1; }
    case "$(uname -m)" in
        x86_64|amd64) arch=amd64 ;;
        aarch64|arm64) arch=arm64 ;;
        *) echo 'Supported architectures: x86-64 and ARM64.' >&2; exit 1 ;;
    esac
    for tool in curl sha256sum mktemp awk; do
        command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Required command missing: $tool" >&2; exit 1; }
    done
    stage=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/tuxee-install.XXXXXXXX")
    trap 'rm -rf "$stage"' 0
    trap 'exit 1' HUP INT TERM
    tag=${1:-}
    if [ -z "$tag" ]; then
        latest=$(curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 30 --max-redirs 5 \
            -o /dev/null -w '%{url_effective}' https://github.com/agent0ai/tuxee/releases/latest)
        tag=${latest##*/}
    fi
    tag=v${tag#v}
    printf '%s\n' "$tag" | awk '/^v(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$/ { ok=1 } END { exit !ok }' ||
        { echo 'Expected a stable version such as v1.2.3.' >&2; exit 1; }
    base=https://github.com/agent0ai/tuxee/releases/download/$tag
    name=tuxee-linux-$arch
    echo "Downloading Tuxee $tag for Linux/$arch..."
    download "$base/checksums.txt" "$stage/checksums.txt" 1048576
    download "$base/$name" "$stage/$name" 134217728
    expected=$(awk -v name="$name" '$2 == name { if (NF != 2 || ++n > 1 || length($1) != 64 || $1 ~ /[^0-9a-fA-F]/) exit 1; hash=tolower($1) } END { if (n != 1) exit 1; print hash }' "$stage/checksums.txt")
    actual=$(sha256sum "$stage/$name" | awk '{print $1}')
    [ "$actual" = "$expected" ] || { echo 'Checksum mismatch; installation unchanged.' >&2; exit 1; }
    chmod 700 "$stage/$name"
    [ "$("$stage/$name" version)" = "Tuxee ${tag#v}" ] ||
        { echo 'Binary cannot run here. Check glibc/PAM compatibility; installation unchanged.' >&2; exit 1; }
    "$stage/$name" __install
}

download() (
    # Bound streamed bodies even when the server omits Content-Length.
    ulimit -f 262144
    curl -fSL --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 --max-redirs 5 \
        --max-filesize "$3" -o "$2" "$1"
    [ "$(wc -c < "$2")" -le "$3" ]
)

# Parse the complete script before doing work when piped into sh.
main "$@"

# Container startup scripts

Place Bash scripts in `/init`, for example `my-service.sh` and `another-service.sh`.
On every container start or restart, a background job launches all top-level
`*.sh` files independently in parallel alongside Tuxee. Tuxee starts independently
and never waits for these scripts. There is no execution order guarantee; put
dependent preparation and startup commands in the same script. An empty folder is fine.

Scripts run as root inside the container, each in a separate Bash process with
`/init` as its working directory. They do not need executable permission. Hidden
files, subdirectories, Markdown and other file types are ignored. Environment
changes in one script do not carry over to other scripts or Tuxee.
Root password initialization finishes before scripts start; `ROOT_PASSWORD` is
removed from their environment.

Scripts may run forever. One script blocking, exiting or crashing does not stop
the others or Tuxee. Failures are reported in the container logs. Make scripts
safe to run repeatedly.
The init runner runs once per container start, without automatic restart;
restarting Tuxee alone does not rerun it. Completed or failed scripts stay stopped
until the next container start. On shutdown, the runner terminates each script's
process group, including its child processes. Native Tuxee installations do not
use this folder.

## Start a service that stays running

Run a service directly in the foreground. For example, save this as
`/init/my-service.sh`, after placing your application in `/root/my-service`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -e
cd /root/my-service
exec ./server
```

To restart a program whenever it exits, keep a loop in its script:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
cd /root/my-service || exit 1
trap 'exit 0' INT TERM
while true; do
    ./server || true
    sleep 1
done
```

Keep services in the foreground; the init runner already launches each script
in the background. The one-second delay avoids a tight loop if startup fails.

Install any dependencies your service needs. Node, npm and PM2 are not bundled.
Tuxee has its own restart loop with a one-second delay.

Service output and init failures appear in `docker compose logs -f tuxee`.
Publish any additional service ports in your Docker configuration.

## Keep your scripts

The supplied Compose configuration stores `/init` in the `tuxee-init` volume,
so scripts survive container recreation and can be edited in Tuxee's file browser.
For host-managed scripts, replace that volume mount with `./my-init:/init` (add
`:ro` if you only want to edit them on the host). A bind mount hides this bundled
README; copy it into your host folder if you want to keep it visible.

Restart the container to run changed scripts.
